memories.content: Specify a single representative measure that serves as the criterion for retaining, modifying, or discarding compared design alternatives.
HCI review panels verify whether clear criteria for judging design alternatives are established using the declared primary measure.
Collect process measures to diagnose interaction steps where problems occurred, alongside the primary outcome measure.
Interpret evaluation results as differences between compared design alternatives rather than as success or failure of a single prototype.
Check boundary cases to verify whether the derived design principles retain explanatory power for adjacent situations not included in the comparison.
Controlled evaluation environments do not reproduce time pressure, peer intervention, or voluntary termination conditions found in daily use.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains. The reference covers comparative design evaluation and validity, while the compared frame covers participant-compensation fairness, calculation, payment, and classification; neither supplies a counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes a primary measure as the decision criterion for design alternatives.
relations.summary: A single representative measure should determine whether compared design alternatives are retained, modified, or discarded.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame assigns review panels this verification responsibility.
relations.summary: HCI review panels verify that declared primary measures provide clear criteria for judging design alternatives.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame requires diagnostic process measures alongside the primary outcome.
relations.summary: Process measures should accompany the primary outcome measure to locate problematic interaction steps.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame states this comparative interpretation rule.
relations.summary: Evaluation results should be interpreted as differences among alternatives rather than as a single prototype’s success or failure.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame requires testing derived principles against adjacent situations.
relations.summary: Adjacent boundary cases should test whether derived design principles retain explanatory power beyond the original comparison.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame identifies these external-validity limitations.
relations.summary: Controlled evaluations omit daily-use conditions such as time pressure, peer intervention, and voluntary termination.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame defines this burden-based budgeting method.
relations.summary: Research compensation budgets should reflect session time plus required technical and travel preparation.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame governs compensation following mid-study withdrawal.
relations.summary: Participants who withdraw midway should be compensated for their actual participation time.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame establishes modality-independent payment for time spent in sessions.
relations.summary: Actual session time should be compensated regardless of research modality.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame provides this alternative payment method.
relations.summary: Remote participants unable to use electronic transfers may receive equivalent-value gift cards.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame defines how payment-method uncertainty affects proposal review.
relations.summary: An unresolved payment method should not count as a proposal-stage deficiency.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame permits modality-based amount differences tied to participation burden.
relations.summary: On-site and remote compensation may differ when travel or technical-preparation burdens differ.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame states how participants judge compensation fairness.
relations.summary: Participants assess compensation fairness from the combined burden of session time and required preparation.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame addresses compensation for longitudinal out-of-session recording.
relations.summary: Longitudinal-study compensation should include time spent on diary entries and repeated reporting outside sessions.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame requires separating participant payments from staff labor costs.
relations.summary: Participant compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff providing installation and operational support.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame identifies this recurring omission in burden calculations.
relations.summary: Compensation planning commonly counts session time while omitting advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame addresses burden-based participant compensation, special participation conditions, payment methods, proposal review, staff-cost separation, and commonly omitted participant effort.
reports.reference_only: The reference specifies comparative design criteria, diagnostic measures, result interpretation, boundary testing, review oversight, and limits of controlled environments.
